title: XPENG X-World 1.6: Virtual City for AI Driving Tests
summary: XPENG's X-World 1.6 adds Virtual City, rebuilding real roads as repeatable AI test environments, with a 20.9% cut in trajectory endpoint error over version 1.0.
body_markdown:
- **Virtual City enables XPENG to recreate real-world driving environments, revisit challenging scenarios and explore alternative driving outcomes.**
- **X-World 1.6 improves simulation accuracy and consistency, achieving a 20.9% reduction in average trajectory endpoint error compared with X-World 1.0 in internal evaluations.**
- **Real-time interactive simulation and virtual testing capabilities support the training and validation of XPENG's second-generation VLA driving AI.**


**GUANGZHOU, China, November 23, 2026** — XPENG has introduced a major upgrade to X-World, its in-house AI world model designed to support the development and validation of intelligent driving technology. The latest version, X-World 1.6, brings significant improvements in real-world scene reconstruction, simulation accuracy and controllability, making virtual driving environments more practical for AI development.
At the heart of the upgrade is **Virtual City** , a new capability that allows engineers to recreate real-world driving environments, revisit recorded scenarios and explore alternative outcomes. Together with advances in real-time interaction across the X-World platform, these developments enable XPENG to test and refine its intelligent driving technology in more controlled and repeatable virtual environments.


## Recreating Real Roads with Virtual City


One of the greatest challenges in developing intelligent driving systems is reproducing complex, unpredictable situations encountered on public roads. A pedestrian suddenly crossing an intersection or a vehicle making an unexpected manoeuvre may happen only once, making it difficult to recreate identical conditions for repeated testing.
X-World 1.6 addresses this challenge by combining generative AI with real-world scene reconstruction. Using recorded driving data, the model can preserve key elements of a location, such as roads, buildings and surrounding infrastructure, while generating changes in traffic, weather and vehicle movements.
Through Virtual City, XPENG can build virtual representations of real-world locations with spatial and temporal memory, allowing engineers to revisit recorded environments at different points in time and simulate alternative driving scenarios.
For example, engineers can return to the same intersection, introduce different traffic behaviours and test how an AI driving system responds. They can also revisit previously recorded situations to assess whether an updated driving model handles them more effectively. This turns real-world driving experiences into repeatable virtual tests, enabling more consistent evaluation of AI performance.


*X-World can generate seven camera views from a single street-view image, enabling dynamic driving scene prediction.*


## Improving Simulation Accuracy and Real-Time Interaction


Beyond recreating real environments, X-World 1.6 significantly improves simulation consistency and controllability. Earlier generative world models could produce realistic driving scenes, but maintaining consistency across repeated simulations remained challenging. Roadside structures or traffic signals could change unexpectedly, making it difficult to compare results.
The upgraded X-World addresses these limitations by keeping the underlying environment stable while allowing dynamic elements to change. According to XPENG's published technical research, X-World 1.6 achieved a **20.9% reduction in average trajectory endpoint error compared with X-World 1.0** in internal evaluations, demonstrating improved alignment between simulated and reference vehicle trajectories.
XPENG has also advanced real-time interaction across the X-World platform. Engineers can use a steering wheel and pedals to drive through AI-generated environments, with the virtual world responding to their actions. This allows them to explore challenging situations, including sudden braking, sharp turns and unexpected vehicle movements, helping evaluate the model's behaviour beyond ordinary driving conditions.


*Comparison of real-world footage (ground truth), X-World 1.0 and X-World 1.6, demonstrating improved accuracy and consistency in scene reconstruction.*


## Supporting the Development of VLA 2.0


X-World plays an important role in the development of XPENG's second-generation VLA driving AI, supporting closed-loop simulation, AI training and driving data generation.
Unlike conventional simulation based on predefined scenarios, X-World enables AI driving models to interact with generated environments, make driving decisions and experience the consequences of those decisions.
Its ability to recreate and modify real-world scenarios also helps engineers test rare or challenging driving situations that are difficult to reproduce consistently on public roads. These capabilities support more efficient development and validation of intelligent driving systems while complementing real-world testing.
As XPENG continues to advance its Physical AI technologies, X-World represents a key part of the company's in-house AI development infrastructure, connecting real-world driving data with virtual simulation to support the continuous improvement of its intelligent driving technology.
